passages.subject: retail / self-checkout machines
passages.text: Self-checkout machines were introduced to save supermarkets money, but their true cost has turned out to be harder to calculate. At first sight, the logic seems obvious. One assistant can supervise six machines, so a store needs fewer staff at the tills. However, the arrangement shifts part of the work to the customer, who now scans, weighs and packs the goods without being paid for it. Many shoppers accept this because it feels faster, especially when they buy only a few items. With a full trolley, the experience is often slower and more frustrating. A more serious problem for retailers is theft. Some customers deliberately skip items, while others inadvertently make mistakes that are difficult to discern from dishonesty. Studies suggest that the losses incurred at self-service tills are substantially higher than at staffed ones. In some stores they are high enough to offset most of the savings on wages. Several chains have therefore reduced the number of machines or limited them to small baskets in order to curb theft. Others have added cameras and weighing systems. These, in turn, annoy honest customers when an alarm is triggered by mistake. The underlying lesson is not that self-checkout has failed. It is that a technology which simply transfers a task from one person to another rarely removes its costs. More often, it moves them to a place where they are harder to see. Whether a store deems the machines a success therefore depends on what it chooses to count.

passages.subject: social psychology / the bystander effect
passages.text: For decades, psychology textbooks have taught that people are less likely to help in an emergency when many others are present. Research on this so-called bystander effect began after a murder in New York in 1964, when newspapers claimed that dozens of neighbours had simply watched. Later investigations showed that these reports had distorted the facts, since few neighbours had seen the attack and some had tried to help. Nevertheless, the notion became firmly established, and laboratory experiments seemed to reinforce it. In these studies, participants who believed that others were nearby responded more slowly to a staged emergency. The underlying explanation was that the presence of others inhibits action, because responsibility is divided among everyone present. Recent research has examined real conflicts recorded by street cameras in three countries. It found that in nine out of ten cases at least one bystander intervened. Moreover, help became more likely, not less, as the number of people grew. These findings do not necessarily contradict the earlier experiments. Each individual may still be slightly less inclined to act in a crowd. However, a larger group is also more likely to contain someone willing to step in, so the chance that nobody helps becomes negligible. Real conflicts also differ from laboratory tests, because they often involve friends rather than strangers. The lesson is not that the early research was worthless. It is that a finding which seems compelling in the laboratory may be a poor guide to behaviour in public. A dramatic story can also perpetuate a belief long after its factual basis has eroded.

passages.subject: law / plain-language legal writing
passages.text: Legal documents are famously difficult to read, and many people sign contracts that they do not fully understand. This problem has prompted several countries to pass laws requiring consumer contracts and official letters to be written in plain language. The idea is simple. If citizens are expected to comply with rules, they should be able to understand them without hiring a lawyer. Many lawyers have resisted this movement. They argue that traditional legal phrases have a precise meaning that courts have established over centuries. Replacing them, they claim, may make a text ambiguous, because a familiar word can seem clearer to a reader while being less exact in court. Supporters of plain language concede that this risk exists, but they believe it is exaggerated. Studies of rewritten documents show that clear versions are easier to understand and also lead to fewer disputes, because both sides know what they agreed to. Moreover, much of the complexity of legal writing has nothing to do with precision. Long sentences, double negatives and needless repetition render a text harder to read without making it more exact. Removing them does not change the legal meaning at all. The debate has gradually become less contentious. It has shifted from whether plain language is possible to how it should be done. Most experts now accept that some technical terms are indispensable. However, they insist that such terms should be explained explicitly, so that readers are not deprived of the information they need to make a decision.

passages.subject: urban sociology / artists and gentrification
passages.text: Artists are often the first newcomers to move into a poor urban neighbourhood, and they are frequently blamed for what follows. The pattern is familiar in many cities. Low rents attract painters, musicians and designers, who open studios in old warehouses and empty shops. Cafés and galleries follow, the area gains a reputation, and wealthier residents begin to arrive. Rents rise, and eventually both the original residents and the artists themselves can no longer afford to stay. Critics argue that artists inadvertently prepare a neighbourhood for investors. Researchers, however, have found that the relationship is more complicated and the evidence less compelling than critics assume. In many cases, the decisive factors were decisions made by city governments and developers, such as new transport links or changes to planning rules. Artists may make a district more visible, but they rarely have the money to transform it. Some studies even suggest that neighbourhoods with a large artistic population change less than others, because a strong local identity can constrain commercial pressure. This does not mean that artists bear no responsibility. Their presence can facilitate a process that is already under way. However, blaming individual newcomers diverts attention from the policies that determine who can afford to live where. A narrow focus on artists may even perpetuate the problem that it criticises. Several cities now try to protect affordable studio space directly. They believe that the issue is economic rather than cultural, and that only substantial public action can mitigate it.

passages.subject: economics / luxury goods and price
passages.text: Most products sell less when their price goes up, but some luxury goods behave in the opposite way. For a handbag or a watch from a famous brand, the usual rule does not prevail, and a higher price can actually increase demand. Economists explain this apparent paradox by pointing out that the buyer is paying for more than the object. Part of what is being bought is a conspicuous message that the owner can afford it. If the price falls, the message weakens, and some customers lose interest. This explains several practices that would otherwise be deemed irrational. Luxury firms rarely hold sales, and some have destroyed unsold stock rather than offer it at a discount. They also curb supply, so that certain items can only be bought after a long wait. Such strategies make sense only if scarcity is part of the value and the brand can sustain an image of rarity. However, the effect has clear limits. A brand that raises its prices too far, or becomes too common, risks losing the very exclusivity it depends on. Counterfeit goods are expected to undermine this exclusivity, because they allow people to display the sign without paying for it. Interestingly, research suggests that fakes do not always harm the original brand. Some buyers of copies later purchase the real product, and the wide visibility of copies can reinforce the brand's prestige. The relationship between price and desire is therefore more fragile than it appears. It depends heavily on how the product is perceived by others.

questions.subject: urban transport / rental e-scooters
questions.stem: Although rental e-scooters were promoted by city councils as a way of replacing short car journeys, ----.

options.o1: surveys show that most riders would otherwise have walked or taken the bus
options.o2: surveys show that most riders would otherwise have made the same journey by car
options.o3: the scooters must be parked in marked areas in most city centres
options.o4: riders are required to be at least eighteen years old
options.o5: the batteries are usually collected and charged during the night

questions.why: Although bir ödün bağlacıdır: amaç araba yolculuklarının yerini almaktı, ama scooterlar yürüyüşün ve otobüsün yerini almıştır.
questions.trap_note: Amacın gerçekleştiğini söyler; ödün bağlacından sonra beklenenin tersi gelmelidir.

questions.subject: public transport / night buses
questions.stem: Cities that cut their night bus services in order to save money often discover that the savings are offset by ----.

options.o1: the higher cost of the problems that arise when shift workers cannot get home safely
options.o2: the lower number of passengers who travel by bus during the evening rush hour
options.o3: the decision of several drivers to retire earlier than they had planned
options.o4: the popularity of cycling among students who live in the centre
options.o5: the price of the new buses bought for the daytime routes

questions.why: be offset by 'tarafından dengelenmek, götürülmek' demektir: tasarrufu silen şey, gece işçilerinin eve dönememesinin doğurduğu daha büyük maliyettir.
questions.trap_note: Bir tasarrufu dengeleyecek bir maliyet değil, akşam saatlerine ait ilgisiz bir azalma söyler; gece hatlarıyla bağı yoktur.

questions.subject: health services / hospital parking charges
questions.stem: Critics of hospital parking charges argue that the fees fall most heavily on the people who are least able to avoid them, such as ----.

options.o1: patients who need frequent treatment and relatives who visit every day
options.o2: visitors who come only once and stay for less than an hour
options.o3: members of staff who live within walking distance of the hospital
options.o4: drivers who choose to park in the streets nearby
options.o5: companies that deliver medical supplies to the hospital

questions.why: such as bir örnek ister: ücretten kaçamayan ve en çok ödeyenler sık tedavi gören hastalar ile her gün gelen yakınlardır.
questions.trap_note: En az etkilenecek grubu örnek verir; bir kez gelip kısa kalan ziyaretçi ücretin yükünü en az taşıyandır.

questions.subject: leisure / theme park fast passes
questions.stem: Theme parks that sell tickets allowing visitors to skip the queues can raise a great deal of extra money, but they also risk ----.

options.o1: provoking resentment among the visitors who are left waiting even longer
options.o2: reducing the waiting time for every single visitor in the park
options.o3: attracting more families who live close to the park
options.o4: encouraging visitors to buy their food inside the park
options.o5: selling more tickets during the summer holidays

questions.why: but bir sakınca ister: sırayı atlayanlar yüzünden ötekiler daha uzun bekler ve bu onların öfkesine yol açar (provoke resentment).
questions.trap_note: Sırayı atlamak herkesin beklemesini kısaltamaz; ötekilerin süresini uzatır. Seçenek hem mantıkla hem de but ile çelişir.

questions.subject: education / private tutoring
questions.stem: Because private tutoring is bought mainly by families who can already afford many other advantages for their children, ----.

options.o1: its rapid growth may widen rather than narrow the gap between pupils
options.o2: its rapid growth is likely to narrow the gap between rich and poor pupils
options.o3: tutors are usually paid by the hour rather than by the month
options.o4: many tutors are university students looking for extra income
options.o5: most lessons now take place online in the evenings

questions.why: Ek dersi zaten avantajlı aileler satın alıyorsa, büyümesi aradaki farkı kapatmaz, açar.
questions.trap_note: Öncülün sonucunu tersine çevirir; avantajlı aileye giden kaynak farkı daraltamaz.

questions.subject: technology / open-source volunteers
questions.stem: Much of the software that large companies depend on every day is maintained by a handful of unpaid volunteers, which means that ----.

options.o1: a vital system can become vulnerable when a single tired volunteer stops working on it
options.o2: a vital system is protected by the large teams that companies employ to look after it
options.o3: the code is usually written in several different programming languages
options.o4: volunteers are often students who want to improve their skills
options.o5: companies are legally required to publish the software they use

questions.why: Sistem bir avuç ücretsiz gönüllüye dayanıyorsa, biri bırakınca savunmasız (vulnerable) kalır.
questions.trap_note: Öncülle çelişir: sistemi büyük şirket ekipleri değil, bir avuç gönüllü ayakta tutmaktadır.

questions.subject: energy / smart meters
questions.stem: Smart meters show households exactly how much energy they are using, yet the savings they produce tend to diminish after the first few months, because ----.

options.o1: people stop looking at the display once the novelty has worn off
options.o2: the price of energy usually falls during the winter months
options.o3: the meters are installed free of charge by the energy companies
options.o4: most households already knew exactly how much they were spending
options.o5: the devices send their readings automatically every half hour

questions.why: diminish 'azalmak' demektir: tasarruf ilk aylardan sonra azalıyorsa, insanlar yeniliği geçince göstergeye bakmayı bırakmıştır.
questions.trap_note: Tasarrufun azalmasını fiyata bağlar; kök ise tüketim davranışından söz eder ve fiyat kışın düşmez.

questions.subject: housing / adults in house-shares
questions.stem: Adults in their thirties are increasingly sharing houses with people they barely know, not because they prefer it but because ----.

options.o1: rents in many cities have risen far faster than their incomes
options.o2: they enjoy the company of strangers more than living alone
options.o3: landlords in most cities prefer to rent to single tenants
options.o4: shared houses are usually located close to the city centre
options.o5: the law requires tenants to sign a contract for at least a year

questions.why: not because A but because B kalıbı gerçek nedeni B'ye verir: kira gelirden hızlı artmıştır.
questions.trap_note: Kökün 'not because they prefer it' diyerek dışladığı nedeni geri getirir.

questions.subject: consumer policy / repairability labels
questions.stem: A label showing how easy a product is to repair gives buyers information that the price alone cannot tell them, and over time this may ----.

options.o1: prompt manufacturers to design products that last longer
options.o2: prompt manufacturers to raise the price of every repair
options.o3: make the product heavier and more expensive to transport
options.o4: reduce the number of shops that sell electronic goods
options.o5: replace the guarantee that comes with the product

questions.why: Alıcı onarılabilirliği görebilirse üreticiler daha uzun ömürlü ürün tasarlamaya yönelir. prompt burada 'yöneltmek, sevk etmek' demektir.
questions.trap_note: Doğru şıkla aynı fiille başlar, bu yüzden göz gezdiren okuru yakalar; ama etiketin amacına ters bir sonuç söyler.

questions.subject: libraries / late-night opening
questions.stem: When the city library extended its opening hours until midnight, the staff expected very few visitors after ten o'clock, but ----.

options.o1: the late hours proved especially popular with students and shift workers
options.o2: very few people came after ten o'clock, exactly as they had predicted
options.o3: the building had been renovated only two years earlier
options.o4: the books on the upper floors were moved to a new storage area
options.o5: the library had already introduced a self-service lending system

questions.why: but beklentinin tersini ister: az ziyaretçi beklenmişti, oysa geç saatler öğrenciler ve vardiyalı çalışanlar arasında çok tuttu.
questions.trap_note: Beklentiyi doğrular; but'tan sonra gelen cümle beklentiyi kırmalıdır.

questions.subject: food / carbon labels
questions.stem: Carbon labels on food packaging are designed to help shoppers make greener choices, but the figures are often too ambiguous to interpret.

options.o1: Gıda ambalajlarındaki karbon etiketleri alışveriş yapanların daha çevreci seçimler yapmasına yardım etmek için tasarlanmıştır, ancak rakamlar çoğu zaman yorumlanamayacak kadar belirsizdir.
options.o2: Gıda ambalajlarındaki karbon etiketleri alışveriş yapanların daha çevreci seçimler yapmasına yardım etmek için tasarlanmıştır ve rakamlar çoğu zaman herkesin anlayabileceği kadar açıktır.
options.o3: Alışveriş yapanlar, daha çevreci seçimler yapabilmek için karbon etiketlerinin konmasını talep etmiştir.
options.o4: Karbon etiketleri gıdaların fiyatını yükselttiği için alışveriş yapanlarca sevilmemektedir.
options.o5: Rakamları yorumlayamayan alışverişçiler karbon etiketli ürünleri satın almamaktadır.

questions.why: too ambiguous to interpret 'yorumlanamayacak kadar belirsiz' demektir; ambiguous 'belirsiz, iki anlama gelebilen' anlamındadır.
questions.trap_note: ambiguous'u 'açık' diye okur ve but ile kurulan karşıtlığı and ile bir onaylamaya çevirir.

questions.subject: road safety / speed cameras
questions.stem: Speed cameras reduce accidents at the places where they are installed, but their effect rarely persists beyond the point where the camera stands.

options.o1: Hız kameraları kuruldukları yerlerde kazaları azaltır, ancak etkileri kameranın bulunduğu noktanın ötesinde nadiren sürer.
options.o2: Hız kameraları kuruldukları yerlerde kazaları azaltır ve etkileri kameranın bulunduğu noktanın çok ötesine kadar sürer.
options.o3: Hız kameralarının bulunduğu yerlerde kazalar giderek artmaktadır.
options.o4: Sürücüler hız kameralarının nerede olduğunu bildikleri için kazalardan kaçınır.
options.o5: Hız kameraları yalnızca kazaların sık yaşandığı noktalara kurulmaktadır.

questions.why: persist 'sürmek' demektir ve rarely ile olumsuzlanır: etki kameranın ötesinde pek sürmez.
questions.trap_note: rarely sözcüğünü atlar; etkinin süreceğini söyleyerek cümlenin uyarısını bir övgüye çevirir.

questions.subject: relationships / dating apps
questions.stem: Dating apps give users far more choice than they had before, yet many users say that such abundant choice makes it harder to commit to one person.

options.o1: Arkadaşlık uygulamaları kullanıcılara eskisinden çok daha fazla seçenek sunar, ancak birçok kullanıcı bu kadar bol seçeneğin tek bir kişiye bağlanmayı zorlaştırdığını söylemektedir.
options.o2: Arkadaşlık uygulamaları kullanıcılara eskisinden çok daha fazla seçenek sunar ve birçok kullanıcı bu kadar bol seçeneğin tek bir kişiye bağlanmayı kolaylaştırdığını söylemektedir.
options.o3: Arkadaşlık uygulamalarını kullananlar eskiden olduğundan daha az seçeneğe sahiptir.
options.o4: Kullanıcılar tek bir kişiye bağlanmak için arkadaşlık uygulamalarını tercih etmektedir.
options.o5: Arkadaşlık uygulamaları kullanıcıların seçeneklerini bilinçli olarak sınırlamaktadır.

questions.why: yet bir karşıtlık kurar: seçenek çoğalmıştır ama bağlanmak zorlaşmıştır. abundant 'bol' demektir.
questions.trap_note: Karşıtlığı kaldırır; 'kolaylaştırdığını' der ve yet'in kurduğu çelişkiyi yok eder.

questions.subject: labour / gig-economy delivery riders
questions.stem: Platformlar teslimat kuryelerini çalışan değil serbest çalışan olarak sınıflandırır; bu da onları hastalık izni ve emeklilik gibi haklardan yoksun bırakır.

options.o1: Platforms classify delivery riders as self-employed rather than as employees, which deprives them of rights such as sick pay and pensions.
options.o2: Platforms classify delivery riders as employees rather than as self-employed, which entitles them to rights such as sick pay and pensions.
options.o3: Delivery riders prefer to be self-employed because they do not need sick pay or pensions.
options.o4: Platforms provide sick pay and pensions only to riders who work full time.
options.o5: Riders who are classified as employees lose the right to choose their own hours.

questions.why: 'yoksun bırakmak' deprive of ile karşılanır; sınıflandırmanın yönü de korunmalıdır: serbest çalışan, çalışan değil.
questions.trap_note: Sınıflandırmayı ve sonucunu birlikte tersine çevirir; kurye bu kez haklara kavuşmuş olur.

questions.subject: family policy / parental leave
questions.stem: Babalara ayrılan izin, annelere devredilemediğinde çok daha fazla kullanılmaktadır.

options.o1: Leave reserved for fathers is used far more when it cannot be transferred to mothers.
options.o2: Leave reserved for fathers is used far more when it can be transferred to mothers.
options.o3: Mothers use more parental leave than fathers in every country.
options.o4: Fathers prefer to transfer their leave to mothers whenever this is allowed.
options.o5: Leave that cannot be transferred is rarely used by either parent.

questions.why: Koşul olumsuzdur: izin annelere devredilemediğinde babalar onu daha çok kullanır.
questions.trap_note: cannot'u can'e çevirir; tek bir sözcük cümlenin bütün bulgusunu tersine döndürür.

questions.subject: work / phased retirement
questions.stem: Kademeli emeklilik, çalışanların bilgilerinin bir gecede kaybolmak yerine yerlerine geçecek kişilere aktarılmasını kolaylaştırır.

options.o1: Phased retirement facilitates the transfer of employees' knowledge to their successors, so that it is not lost overnight.
options.o2: Phased retirement causes employees' knowledge to be lost overnight instead of being transferred to their successors.
options.o3: Employees who retire gradually usually refuse to train the people who replace them.
options.o4: Firms prefer phased retirement because it is cheaper than hiring new staff.
options.o5: Successors learn more from written manuals than from the employees they replace.

questions.why: 'kolaylaştırmak' facilitate ile karşılanır; 'bir gecede kaybolmak yerine' ifadesi kaybın önlendiğini söyler.
questions.trap_note: 'yerine' ile kurulan karşıtlığı tersine çevirir ve emekliliği kaybın nedeni yapar.

questions.stem: According to the passage, self-checkout machines shift part of the work ----.

options.o1: from paid staff to customers who do it without being paid
options.o2: from customers to the assistants who supervise the machines
options.o3: from small shops to large supermarket chains
options.o4: from the tills to the warehouse behind the store
options.o5: from honest customers to the cameras above the tills

questions.why: Metin açıkça yazar: düzen işin bir kısmını müşteriye kaydırır; müşteri ücret almadan tarar, tartar ve paketler.
questions.trap_note: Aktarımın yönünü tersine çevirir; metinde gözetmen işi devralan değil, altı makineyi birden izleyen kişidir.

questions.stem: It is clear from the passage that some losses at self-service tills are hard to deal with because ----.

options.o1: honest mistakes and deliberate theft can be hard to tell apart
options.o2: customers with full trolleys are slower than those with baskets
options.o3: the assistants are not allowed to check customers' bags
options.o4: the cameras record only the customers who skip items
options.o5: most stores have removed their staffed tills completely

questions.why: Metin: bazı müşteriler farkında olmadan (inadvertently) hata yapar ve bu hatalar sahtekârlıktan ayırt edilemez (difficult to discern from dishonesty).
questions.trap_note: Metinde geçen doğru bir bilgidir ama hızla ilgilidir; kayıpların neden zor ele alındığını açıklamaz.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that adding cameras and weighing systems to self-service tills ----.

options.o1: deals with one problem while creating another for honest shoppers
options.o2: has completely removed the problem of theft at these tills
options.o3: was introduced mainly in order to speed up the checkout
options.o4: has made customers more willing to use the machines
options.o5: is cheaper than employing more staff at the tills

questions.why: Metin bu sistemlerin, alarm yanlışlıkla çaldığında dürüst müşteriyi rahatsız ettiğini söyler: bir sorunu çözerken başka bir sorun yaratırlar.
questions.trap_note: Metnin vermediği bir başarıyı uydurur; metin hırsızlığın tamamen bittiğini hiçbir yerde söylemez.

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.o1: Self-checkout often moves costs to places where they are harder to see instead of removing them.
options.o2: Self-checkout machines have failed and are being removed from most supermarkets.
options.o3: Customers prefer self-checkout machines when they buy a large number of items.
options.o4: Theft was the main reason why supermarkets introduced self-checkout machines.
options.o5: Supermarkets should employ more staff to supervise their machines.

questions.why: Metin dersini açıkça verir: bir işi bir kişiden ötekine aktaran teknoloji maliyeti nadiren ortadan kaldırır, onu görünmeyen bir yere taşır.
questions.trap_note: Metnin 'The underlying lesson is not that self-checkout has failed' cümlesiyle doğrudan çelişir.

questions.stem: It is clear from the passage that the newspaper reports of the 1964 murder ----.

options.o1: gave a misleading picture of how the neighbours had behaved
options.o2: were confirmed by the investigations that were carried out later
options.o3: were written by psychologists who had studied the case
options.o4: persuaded the police to change the way they answered calls
options.o5: were ignored by researchers for more than fifty years

questions.why: Metin raporların gerçekleri çarpıttığını (distorted the facts) söyler: saldırıyı gören komşu azdı ve bazıları yardım etmeye çalışmıştı. Gazeteler yanıltıcı bir tablo çizmişti.
questions.trap_note: Sonraki soruşturmalar raporları doğrulamamış, tersine çarpıtıldıklarını göstermiştir; 'investigations' sözcüğünü görüp yönünü okumayan okuru yakalar.

questions.stem: According to the passage, the early laboratory experiments suggested that the presence of other people ----.

options.o1: discourages each person from acting, because the responsibility is divided among them
options.o2: encourages each person to act, because nobody wants to look uncaring in public
options.o3: makes people more likely to call the police than to step in themselves
options.o4: has no effect on how quickly people respond to an emergency
options.o5: matters only when the victim is a friend or a neighbour

questions.why: inhibit 'engellemek, ket vurmak' demektir: başkalarının varlığı harekete geçmeyi engeller, çünkü sorumluluk oradaki herkese bölünür.
questions.trap_note: inhibit'i ters anlayan okurun seçeneğidir; deneylerde katılımcılar başkaları yakındayken daha yavaş tepki vermiştir.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that the camera study and the earlier experiments can both be correct because ----.

options.o1: a crowd may contain more helpers even if each person in it is less likely to act
options.o2: each person in a crowd is more likely to act than a person who is alone
options.o3: the camera study was also carried out in a laboratory
options.o4: the early experiments also recorded real conflicts in the street
options.o5: both studies were carried out in the same three countries

questions.why: Metin iki bulguyu uzlaştırır: kalabalıktaki her birey biraz daha az istekli olabilir, ama kalabalık büyüdükçe içinde yardım edecek birinin bulunma olasılığı artar.
questions.trap_note: Grubun bulgusunu bireye taşır; metin tersine her bireyin kalabalıkta biraz daha az istekli olabileceğini söyler. Göz gezdirerek okuyanın en sık düştüğü tuzaktır.

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.o1: A famous psychological finding is a weaker guide to real behaviour than its reputation suggests.
options.o2: The early research on the bystander effect was worthless and should no longer be taught.
options.o3: Street cameras should be installed in every city in order to reduce crime.
options.o4: Newspapers report emergencies more accurately than psychologists do.
options.o5: People in large crowds never help strangers who are in danger.

questions.why: Metin ünlü bir bulgunun kökenini, gerçek kayıtlarla çelişkisini ve laboratuvarın sınırını anlatır; dersi de açıkça verir: laboratuvarda ikna edici (compelling) görünen bir bulgu toplum içindeki davranışa zayıf bir rehber olabilir.
questions.trap_note: Metnin 'The lesson is not that the early research was worthless' cümlesiyle doğrudan çelişir.

questions.stem: According to the passage, many lawyers resist plain language because ----.

options.o1: everyday words may be less exact in court than established legal phrases
options.o2: plain language makes contracts far too long to read
options.o3: citizens prefer to hire a lawyer in any case
options.o4: courts refuse to accept documents written in plain language
options.o5: traditional legal phrases are easier for the public to understand

questions.why: Metin avukatların gerekçesini verir: tanıdık bir sözcük okura açık görünse de mahkemede daha az kesin olabilir.
questions.trap_note: Metinde geçmeyen bir itiraz uydurur; uzunluk avukatların değil, sade dil savunucularının eleştirdiği bir kusurdur.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that removing double negatives and needless repetition from a legal text ----.

options.o1: makes it easier to read without weakening it in court
options.o2: changes the legal meaning of the text in important ways
options.o3: is opposed by most supporters of plain language
options.o4: makes the text longer but more precise
options.o5: is now required by law in most countries

questions.why: Metin bu ögelerin metni daha kesin yapmadan okunmasını zorlaştırdığını (render) söyler; onları çıkarmak hukuki anlamı değiştirmez.
questions.trap_note: Metnin 'Removing them does not change the legal meaning at all' cümlesiyle doğrudan çelişir.

questions.stem: It is clear from the passage that supporters of plain language ----.

options.o1: accept that there is some risk but think it has been overstated
options.o2: deny that replacing legal phrases carries any risk at all
options.o3: want every technical term to be removed from contracts
options.o4: believe that courts should stop using traditional phrases
options.o5: are mostly lawyers who specialise in consumer law

questions.why: concede 'kabul etmek, teslim etmek' demektir: savunucular riskin var olduğunu kabul eder ama abartıldığına inanır.
questions.trap_note: concede'i 'reddetmek' sanan okurun seçeceği şıktır; metin riskin varlığını kabul eder.

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.o1: Legal texts can be made much clearer without losing precision, as long as necessary technical terms are explained.
options.o2: Lawyers should stop using technical terms in all legal documents.
options.o3: Plain-language laws have caused more disputes than they have prevented.
options.o4: Consumers should always hire a lawyer before they sign a contract.
options.o5: Traditional legal phrases are more precise than any alternative.

questions.why: Metin karmaşıklığın çoğunun kesinlikle ilgisi olmadığını söyler ve bazı terimlerin vazgeçilmez olduğunu, ama açıklanması gerektiğini ekler.
questions.trap_note: Metnin son bölümüyle çelişir: uzmanlar bazı teknik terimlerin vazgeçilmez (indispensable) olduğunu kabul eder.

questions.stem: It is clear from the passage that artists move into poor neighbourhoods mainly because ----.

options.o1: the rents there are low
options.o2: investors invite them to make the area attractive
options.o3: the city government gives them free studios
options.o4: wealthier residents have already arrived
options.o5: cafés and galleries have opened nearby

questions.why: Metin ilk adımı açıkça yazar: düşük kiralar ressamları, müzisyenleri ve tasarımcıları çeker.
questions.trap_note: Eleştirmenlerin iddiasını sanatçıların amacı sanır; metinde yatırımcılar sanatçıları davet etmez.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that neighbourhoods with a large number of artists ----.

options.o1: may resist commercial change better than some other areas
options.o2: always change faster than neighbourhoods without artists
options.o3: receive new transport links before other districts
options.o4: are usually the first to be chosen by developers
options.o5: lose their artists before their original residents

questions.why: Metin: güçlü bir yerel kimlik ticari baskıyı sınırlayabilir (constrain). Bu yüzden bu tür semtler daha az değişebilir.
questions.trap_note: Eleştirmenlerin varsayımını genel kural yapar; metin tam tersine bazı araştırmaların daha az değişim bulduğunu söyler.

questions.stem: According to the passage, researchers found that the decisive factors in many cases were ----.

options.o1: decisions taken by city governments and developers
options.o2: the arrival of painters, musicians and designers
options.o3: the reputation of the cafés and galleries
options.o4: the wishes of the original residents
options.o5: the number of empty warehouses in the area

questions.why: Metin belirleyici etkenleri sayar: yeni ulaşım bağlantıları ya da imar kurallarındaki değişiklikler gibi belediye ve müteahhit kararları.
questions.trap_note: Metnin başındaki süreçten sözcük alır; ama araştırmacılar tam da sanatçıların gelişini belirleyici saymamıştır.

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.o1: Artists are blamed for gentrification more than the evidence supports, and the main causes are economic and political.
options.o2: Artists are the main cause of rising rents in poor urban neighbourhoods.
options.o3: Cities should stop artists from opening studios in old warehouses.
options.o4: Neighbourhoods with many artists never change at all.
options.o5: Wealthier residents prefer to live in areas without artists.

questions.why: Metin eleştiriyi aktarır, kanıtın sanıldığından zayıf olduğunu gösterir ve sorunun ekonomik olduğunu söyleyerek biter.
questions.trap_note: Metnin çürütmeye çalıştığı suçlamayı ana fikir yapar.

questions.stem: According to the passage, when the price of some luxury goods falls ----.

options.o1: some customers lose interest because the message they are buying weakens
options.o2: demand rises because many more people can now afford them
options.o3: the firm destroys its unsold stock at once
options.o4: counterfeit goods become more common
options.o5: the brand's prestige is reinforced

questions.why: Metin: fiyat düşerse ileti zayıflar ve bazı müşteriler ilgisini kaybeder.
questions.trap_note: Sıradan malların kuralını uygular; metnin bütün konusu bu kuralın bazı lüks mallarda işlemediğidir.

questions.stem: It is clear from the passage that luxury firms restrict the supply of certain items because ----.

options.o1: scarcity itself is part of what customers are paying for
options.o2: they are unable to produce enough to meet the demand
options.o3: the materials they use are extremely rare
options.o4: they want to reduce the cost of storing unsold stock
options.o5: counterfeiters would otherwise copy their products

questions.why: Kökteki 'restrict supply' metindeki 'curb supply' ifadesinin karşılığıdır; metin bunun ancak kıtlık değerin bir parçasıysa anlamlı olduğunu söyler.
questions.trap_note: Arzın kısılmasını bir üretim yetersizliği sanır; metne göre bu bilinçli bir stratejidir.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that counterfeit goods ----.

options.o1: can sometimes benefit the brands they imitate
options.o2: always destroy the value of the original brand
options.o3: are bought mainly by people who own the real product
options.o4: are more expensive to produce than the originals
options.o5: force luxury firms to lower their prices

questions.why: Metin sahtelerin özgünlüğü baltalaması (undermine) beklendiğini söyler; ama araştırmalara göre bazı alıcılar sonra gerçeğini alır ve kopyalar markanın prestijini pekiştirebilir (reinforce).
questions.trap_note: Beklentiyi bulgu sanır; metin 'fakes do not always harm the original brand' diyerek bunu düzeltir.

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.o1: For some luxury goods a high price is part of the value, although this effect has limits and depends on how others see the product.
options.o2: Luxury goods always become more popular when their prices rise.
options.o3: Counterfeit goods are the greatest threat to the luxury industry.
options.o4: Luxury firms should hold more sales in order to attract new customers.
options.o5: Economists are unable to explain why people buy luxury goods.

questions.why: Metin etkiyi açıklar, sınırlarını sayar ve başkalarının ürünü nasıl algıladığına bağlı olduğunu söyleyerek biter.
questions.trap_note: Metnin 'the effect has clear limits' saptamasını yok sayar ve 'always' ile aşırı genelleme yapar.

questions.subject: childhood / walking to school alone
dialogue: Thirty years ago, most children in this country walked to school on their own. Today very few do. Have the streets become more dangerous?
The way parents perceive the risk. A single frightening story now reaches every family within hours, and no parent wants to be deemed careless by the others.

options.o1: If anything, they have become safer. Far fewer children are hurt on the roads today than in the past.
options.o2: Yes, and that is why parents are right to drive their children to school.
options.o3: Most schools now start later in the morning than they used to.
options.o4: Children today spend more hours at school than their parents did.
options.o5: Many schools now offer breakfast before the first lesson begins.

questions.why: Sunucu ardından 'Peki ne değişti?' diye sorar ve yanıt 'ebeveynlerin riski algılama biçimi' olur; demek ki araştırmacı önce sokakların daha tehlikeli olmadığını söylemiştir.
questions.trap_note: Sunucunun varsayımını onaylar; ama o zaman son replikteki 'değişen, riskin algılanışıdır' yanıtı anlamsız kalır.

questions.subject: public health / the sugar tax
dialogue: When the tax on sugary drinks was introduced, critics said that people would simply pay more and keep drinking the same amount. Were they right?
Partly. People still buy soft drinks in large quantities. But before the tax even started, most manufacturers had already cut the sugar in their recipes.
Why would they do that before they had to pay anything?

options.o1: Because the tax applied only above a certain level of sugar, so a recipe that stayed below that threshold was exempt.
options.o2: Because the tax was so small that it made no difference to their prices at all.
options.o3: Because sugary drinks are more popular in summer than in winter.
options.o4: Because most of their customers had started to prefer drinks in glass bottles.
options.o5: Because the price of sugar on world markets had fallen sharply.

questions.why: Vergi yalnızca belli bir şeker eşiğinin (threshold) üstüne uygulanıyorsa, tarifini eşiğin altına indiren üretici vergiden muaf (exempt) olur; bu yüzden şekeri vergi başlamadan azaltmışlardır.
questions.trap_note: Vergi fiyatı hiç etkilemeseydi üreticilerin tarif değiştirmesi için bir neden kalmazdı; seçenek sorulan 'neden'i açıklamak yerine onu anlamsızlaştırır.

questions.subject: games / chess and computers
dialogue: Quite the opposite. More people play now than at any time in history, and many of them are teenagers.
Why hasn't the computer taken the fun out of the game?
Because people never played in order to be better than a machine. A program shows any beginner exactly where they went wrong, and that has made the game far easier to learn.

options.o1: Now that computers can beat any human player, has interest in chess declined?
options.o2: Do you think computers will one day be able to beat the best human players?
options.o3: How many hours a day do you spend practising?
options.o4: Which opening would you recommend to a complete beginner?
options.o5: Where will the next world championship be held?

questions.why: Yanıt 'Tam tersi' diye başlar ve satrancın hiç bu kadar çok oynanmadığını söyler; boşluk ilginin azalıp azalmadığını sormalıdır. Üçüncü replik de bilgisayarın zaten üstün olduğunu varsayar.
questions.trap_note: Bilgisayarın insanı yenmesini geleceğe koyar; oysa üçüncü replik bunun çoktan gerçekleştiğini varsayar ve 'Quite the opposite' bu soruya yanıt olmaz.

questions.subject: law / emoji in contracts
dialogue: A court in Canada decided that a farmer who replied to a contract with a thumbs-up emoji had accepted it. Isn't that a strange decision?
Less strange than it sounds. The farmer had replied to earlier contracts from the same buyer with short messages such as 'ok' or 'looks good', and the court treated the emoji in the same way.
Not every one. A heart or a smiling face is far more ambiguous, and a judge would look closely at the whole conversation before deciding what it meant.

options.o1: So will any emoji now count as a signature?
options.o2: So the farmer had never sent short replies like that before?
options.o3: How long did it take for the case to reach the court?
options.o4: What was the contract actually for?
options.o5: Do you use emoji in your own work messages?

questions.why: Avukatın 'Hepsi değil' diye başlayan yanıtı, bundan sonra her emojinin imza sayılıp sayılmayacağını soran bir soruya uyar.
questions.trap_note: Avukatın ikinci replikte söylediğiyle çelişir: çiftçi aynı alıcıya daha önce de 'ok' gibi kısa yanıtlar vermiştir.

questions.subject: food / insects as food
dialogue: Insects are often called the food of the future, because farming them needs so little land and water. Will people in Europe ever accept them?
Many already eat insects without knowing it. A red colouring made from insects has been added to sweets and drinks for decades.
But eating a whole insect is surely a different matter?

options.o1: It is, which is why most producers grind them into a flour that is hard to discern in a biscuit or a plate of pasta.
options.o2: Not at all, which is why whole insects are now sold in most European supermarkets.
options.o3: Insects contain more protein than many kinds of meat.
options.o4: Farming insects needs very little land and water.
options.o5: Some people are allergic to certain kinds of insects.

questions.why: Bilim insanı 'Öyle' diyerek bütün bir böceğin başka bir şey olduğunu kabul eder ve üreticilerin çözümünü anlatır: böceği, bisküvide fark edilmesi (discern) zor bir una dönüştürmek. Bu, ikinci replikteki 'farkında olmadan yemek' fikriyle de örtüşür.
questions.trap_note: İlk replikteki soruyla çelişir: soru Avrupalıların böceği henüz benimsemediğini varsayar; 'most European supermarkets' iddiası bunu yok sayar.

questions.subject: agriculture / organic farming yields
questions.stem: Because organic farms tend to yield less food per hectare, converting all farmland to organic methods would require far more land.

options.o1: Organic farms usually produce less food on the same area, so a full switch to organic farming would need much more land.
options.o2: Organic farms usually produce more food on the same area, so a full switch to organic farming would need much less land.
options.o3: Organic farms need more land than conventional ones because they cannot use modern machines.
options.o4: Most farmland has already been converted to organic methods.
options.o5: Food from conventional farms is healthier than organic food.

questions.why: yield 'ürün vermek' demektir: organik çiftlikler hektar başına daha az ürün verir, bu yüzden bütün tarım alanını organiğe çevirmek daha çok toprak ister.
questions.trap_note: yield less'i ters okur ve sonucu da buna göre çevirir; kendi içinde tutarlı göründüğü için tehlikelidir.

questions.subject: crime prevention / street lighting
questions.stem: Better street lighting seems to reduce crime even during the day, which suggests that its effect depends less on criminals being seen than on residents taking more pride in their area.

options.o1: Since crime falls even in daylight where street lighting is improved, the effect probably comes more from residents' pride in their area than from better visibility.
options.o2: Since crime falls only at night where street lighting is improved, the effect probably comes from better visibility rather than from residents' pride.
options.o3: Residents who take pride in their area usually ask the council to improve the street lighting.
options.o4: Criminals prefer to operate during the day because the streets are better lit at night.
options.o5: Street lighting reduces crime more in city centres than in residential areas.

questions.why: Suç gündüz de azalıyorsa etki görünürlükten değil, sakinlerin semtleriyle gurur duymasından gelir; depends less on A than on B kalıbı ağırlığı B'ye verir.
questions.trap_note: 'even during the day' ifadesini 'only at night' diye bozar ve less ... than karşılaştırmasını tersine çevirir.

questions.subject: health / daily step counts
questions.stem: Most of the health benefits of walking are gained below a certain threshold, and beyond it each additional thousand steps adds relatively little.

options.o1: Walking more brings fewer and fewer extra benefits once a person has passed a certain number of steps.
options.o2: Walking brings health benefits only after a person has passed a certain number of steps.
options.o3: Most people walk far fewer steps each day than doctors recommend.
options.o4: Walking is less beneficial to health than most other forms of exercise.
options.o5: The health benefits of walking depend mainly on the speed at which people walk.

questions.why: threshold 'eşik' demektir: yararın çoğu belli bir eşiğin altında kazanılır, eşikten sonra her ek bin adım az şey katar.
questions.trap_note: Eşiği yararın başladığı nokta sanır; cümle ise yararın çoğunun eşiğin altında, yani ondan önce kazanıldığını söyler.

questions.subject: science journalism / press releases
questions.stem: Many of the exaggerated health claims that appear in newspapers can be traced back to the press releases issued by the universities where the research was done.

options.o1: The press releases of universities are often the source of the exaggerated health claims that newspapers publish.
options.o2: Newspapers often exaggerate health research, even though the press releases issued by universities describe it accurately.
options.o3: Universities rarely issue press releases about their health research.
options.o4: Most readers no longer trust the health claims that they read in newspapers.
options.o5: Journalists usually contact the researchers before they write about a study.

questions.why: can be traced back to 'kökeni ...'e dayanır' demektir: abartının kaynağı üniversitelerin basın bültenleridir.
questions.trap_note: Suçu yalnızca gazetelere yükler ve bültenleri temize çıkarır; cümle ise abartının bültenlerde başladığını söyler.

questions.subject: consumer psychology / self-assembled furniture
questions.stem: Furniture that customers assemble themselves was first sold to cut costs, since flat boxes are cheaper to transport and store. Researchers have since found an unexpected benefit for the seller. In experiments, people who had built a simple storage box themselves were willing to pay considerably more for it than for an identical box built by someone else. The effect disappeared, however, when participants were stopped before they could finish. ----

options.o1: It seems that people value their own work mainly when the effort has yielded a finished object.
options.o2: This shows that people value an object more when they have spent time on it, whether or not they finish it.
options.o3: Flat boxes also reduce the number of lorries needed for deliveries.
options.o4: Many customers ask a friend to help them when they assemble large items.
options.o5: Some shops offer to assemble the furniture for an extra charge.

questions.why: Boşluk son cümledir ve bir sonuç çıkarmalıdır: iş bitirilmeden kesilince etki kaybolduğuna göre, insanlar emeklerine ancak bu emek bitmiş bir nesne ortaya çıkardığında (yield) değer verir.
questions.trap_note: Hemen önceki cümleyle çelişir: katılımcılar işi bitiremeyince etki ortadan kalkmıştır; 'whether or not they finish' bu bulguyu yok sayar.

questions.subject: geography / place names
questions.stem: ---- In England, towns whose names end in '-by' were usually founded by Scandinavian settlers more than a thousand years ago. Names that contain 'ford' show where travellers could once cross a river on foot. In many cities, street names still record trades that died out centuries ago.

options.o1: Many place names retain information about the past that the people who live there have long forgotten.
options.o2: Most place names in England were changed during the last century to make them easier to spell.
options.o3: Scandinavian languages are still taught in a number of English schools.
options.o4: Rivers have always played an important part in trade and transport.
options.o5: Many English towns grew rapidly after the railway arrived.

questions.why: Boşluk ilk cümledir ve konuyu kurmalıdır: devamındaki üç örnek ('-by', 'ford', sokak adları) yer adlarının unutulmuş bir geçmişi koruduğunu (retain) gösterir.
questions.trap_note: Örneklerin hepsiyle çelişir: adlar değiştirilmiş olsaydı bin yıllık izleri taşımazdı.

questions.subject: colonial history / the Hanoi rat bounty
questions.stem: In 1902, the French authorities in Hanoi tried to reduce the city's rat population by paying residents a small reward for every rat tail they handed in. ---- Before long, however, officials began to notice rats without tails running through the streets. Residents had been cutting off the tails and releasing the animals, so that they could breed and produce more tails. Economists still tell the story to show how a badly designed incentive can produce the opposite of what was intended.

options.o1: At first, the scheme seemed to work, as thousands of tails were brought in every day.
options.o2: As a result, the number of rats in the city fell steadily for many years.
options.o3: Rats were also a serious problem in many European cities at that time.
options.o4: Some residents kept cats in order to protect their stores of food.
options.o5: Today, Hanoi is one of the largest cities in Southeast Asia.

questions.why: Boşluktan sonra 'Before long, however' gelir; demek ki boşluk planın önce işler gibi göründüğünü söylemelidir. Ardından gelen kuyruksuz fareler bu ilk başarıyı bozar.
questions.trap_note: Paragrafın sonuyla çelişir: teşvik (incentive) fareleri azaltmamış, üremelerine yol açmıştır; 'As a result' doğal bir devam gibi görünse de 'however' ile kurulan karşıtlığı yok eder.

questions.subject: urban history / the frozen Thames
questions.stem: Between the seventeenth and early nineteenth centuries, the River Thames in London sometimes froze so thickly that fairs were held on the ice. The winters of that period were certainly colder than those of today. ---- The old London Bridge stood on so many thick stone supports that it acted almost like a dam and slowed the water above it. Slow water freezes far more easily than a fast current. When the bridge was replaced in 1831 and the banks were later narrowed, the river flowed faster, and it has never again frozen solid in the centre of the city.

options.o1: However, cold weather alone does not explain why the river froze so easily.
options.o2: These fairs ended when the winters suddenly became much warmer.
options.o3: London was then one of the largest and busiest cities in Europe.
options.o4: Frost fairs were also held on rivers in several other European cities.
options.o5: The new bridge was designed by a well-known Scottish engineer.

questions.why: Önceki cümle kışların daha soğuk olduğunu söyler, sonraki cümle başka bir nedeni, köprüyü anlatmaya başlar. Boşluk, soğuğun tek başına yetmediğini söyleyerek iki cümleyi bağlamalıdır.
questions.trap_note: Paragrafın açıklamasıyla çelişir: nehrin artık donmaması iklimle değil, köprünün değişmesi ve akıntının hızlanmasıyla açıklanır.

questions.subject: language history / the word OK
sentences: The word 'OK' may be the most widely used expression in the world, yet it began as a joke.
In 1839, a Boston newspaper used it as a short form of 'oll korrect', a deliberately comic misspelling of 'all correct'.
A year later, supporters of a presidential candidate nicknamed 'Old Kinderhook' used it as a slogan, which made it known nationwide.
Many newspapers of that period also printed poems sent in by their readers.
Telegraph operators later found it useful, and from there it spread into almost every language.
questions.why: IV. cümle 'newspapers' sözcüğünü paylaşır ama gazetelerin okur şiirlerine geçer; sözcüğün şakadan sloganla, sonra telgrafla yayılmasını anlatan zinciri koparır.
questions.trap_note: V. cümle telgraf gibi yeni bir konu açtığı için sapma sanılır; oysa yayılma zincirinin son halkasıdır ve I'deki 'en yaygın ifade' iddiasını tamamlar.

questions.subject: food history / the potato in Europe
sentences: When the potato was brought to Europe from South America in the sixteenth century, many people regarded it with suspicion.
Some believed that it caused disease, and in many regions it was grown only as food for animals.
Over the next two centuries, however, governments began to encourage farmers to grow it, because a field of potatoes could feed far more people than a field of wheat.
Historians now believe that the potato played a substantial part in the rapid growth of Europe's population after 1700.
Today, potatoes are grown in more than a hundred countries, and China produces more of them than any other.
questions.why: V. cümle patatesten söz eder ama bugünkü dünya üretimine geçer; paragrafın konusu patatesin Avrupa'da kuşkuyla karşılanıp sonra benimsenmesi ve nüfusa etkisidir.
questions.trap_note: II. cümle hastalık ve hayvan yemi gibi ayrıntılarla konudan sapıyor gibi görünür; oysa I'deki kuşkunun (suspicion) nedenlerini verir ve III'teki 'however' ona dayanır.

questions.subject: television / laugh tracks
sentences: For decades, television comedies were broadcast with recorded laughter, even when they had been filmed without an audience.
Many of the most successful comedies of that period were later sold to television channels in other countries.
Producers believed that hearing others laugh would make viewers find the jokes funnier, and research suggests that they were right.
Laughter is contagious, so people laugh more readily when they hear it, even when they know that it has been recorded.
Many recent comedies have nevertheless abandoned the practice, because audiences increasingly perceive it as an attempt to tell them when to laugh.
questions.why: II. cümle 'comedies' sözcüğünü paylaşır ama dizilerin yurt dışına satışına geçer; kayıtlı kahkahanın neden kullanıldığını ve neden bırakıldığını anlatan zinciri koparır.
questions.trap_note: IV. cümle kahkaha üzerine genel bir bilgi verdiği için sapma sanılır; oysa III'teki araştırma bulgusunun nedenini açıklar.

questions.subject: history of medicine / hand-washing
sentences: In the 1840s, a doctor working in a large hospital in Vienna noticed that far more mothers died after giving birth in one of its wards than in the other.
In the first ward, the doctors often came straight from examining dead bodies, while the second ward was run by midwives who did no such work.
Vienna was then one of the largest cities in Europe, and its university attracted medical students from many countries.
When he made the doctors wash their hands in a chlorine solution, the death rate in the first ward fell dramatically.
Yet many of his colleagues rejected his findings, partly because nobody could yet explain how something invisible could carry disease.
questions.why: III. cümle Viyana ve üniversite sözcükleriyle bağlantılı görünür ama kentin büyüklüğüne geçer; iki koğuş arasındaki farkın nedenini ve el yıkamanın etkisini anlatan zinciri koparır.
questions.trap_note: II. cümle kadavralar ve ebeler gibi yeni ayrıntılar getirdiği için sapma sanılır; oysa IV'teki el yıkama önleminin nedenini veren halkadır.

questions.subject: zoology / zebra stripes
sentences: Scientists have proposed many explanations for the zebra's stripes, from confusing lions to helping the animal keep cool.
Most of these explanations have proved difficult to support with evidence.
In recent experiments, horses wearing striped coats were landed on by far fewer biting flies than horses wearing plain coats.
Zebras live in groups and can run at more than fifty kilometres an hour when they are chased.
This suggests that the stripes protect the animal mainly against insects, which spread serious diseases in the regions where zebras live.
questions.why: IV. cümle zebradan söz eder ama sürü hâlinde yaşamaya ve hıza geçer; III'teki deney ile V'teki 'This suggests' sonucu arasındaki bağı koparır.
questions.trap_note: V. cümle hastalık gibi yeni bir konu açtığı için sapma sanılır; oysa 'This suggests' ile III'teki deneyden sonuç çıkaran halkadır.
